# dsh-composer-plus

> Composer Plus: a community plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh), DeepSeek's open-source agent harness. One install adds Codex-style quality-of-life features to the dsh desktop app and web UI, and iPhone access with the Tether app. npm package: `dsh-composer-plus`. MIT license. Unofficial.

Install in the dsh desktop app: Settings → Plugins → Add plugin → `dsh-composer-plus` → Enable now. Install in a web/CLI profile: `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-composer-plus`, then restart dsh. Requires dsh >= 0.2.0-rc.2 and Node.js >= 22. Tested on dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 (desktop and web) and 0.2.1-rc.2 (web).

Features (each one can be switched off in Settings → Composer Plus):

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED FEATURES: edit docs/features.json, then run npm run build:readme -->
- Changes panel: right sidebar page that opens on a branch map of the chat's repository (counts of all, merged and waiting branches that filter the map; each branch colored by whether the main branch has its work, with an arrow to the branch that merged it or that it started from; remote branches only without a local branch of the same name; a branch opens its newest 300 commits, a commit its files and diffs, the Merged label the merge commit, the Waiting label the files that the branch brings into its target), uncommitted / unstaged / staged / branch git changes and per-file diffs, a "This chat" view (the files that the open chat's file tools wrote in all its turns, with their total diff since its first message) and a switch that hides whitespace-only changes (`git diff -w`); a file's menu lists the chats of the same repository whose write/edit tools changed that file (newest first, with the request; read from the chat logs, rolled-back requests marked) and opens a chat at that request; read-only git.
- Feature ideas: Tinder-style cards on a right sidebar page; on a click, the chat's own model reads a short read-only summary of the project (top-level names, README/manifest heads, an outline of the rest of the README, the titles of recent commits; no .env or key files, no symlink out of the project, no FIFO) and suggests up to 8 features as swipeable cards, written in dsh's UI language. Swipe right (✓ or →) starts a new chat in the same project in plan mode with the idea; ▶ Build now (or ↑) starts the new chat without plan mode, so the model makes the change at once (usual approvals); swipe left (✕ or ←) skips; ↓ (button or key) saves the idea in the project's Later list (kept per project folder under the dsh home, also after a restart; at most 50), where Plan starts the same plan-mode chat and Build now the chat without a plan, and both remove it from the list; Plan all (N) starts one plan-mode chat for every idea in the list and empties it; History keeps every suggested idea of the project (skipped, saved, started; at most 200) and the model never gets them again (Forget allows one again); the buttons and keys fly the card off like a swipe; Undo (Z) brings a card back. An optional focus topic (free text, at most 80 characters, or the fixed chips Performance, Accessibility, Tests, Security, Usability, Documentation) limits the suggestions to that topic; an empty focus sends the same request as before. Copy as checklist (Later list) copies the saved ideas as a Markdown checklist (`- [ ] Title — Summary`) with no network call. Open GitHub issue (Later list) runs the user's own `gh issue create` in the project folder (the gh login of the Mac, the project's GitHub remote) with the idea's title and summary, and keeps the issue link on the idea. No model call before the click; nothing in the project is written.
- Content search: On by default; applies after a dsh restart. The dsh sidebar search (magnifier next to Workspaces, Cmd+K in the desktop app, Cmd+Alt+K in a browser) also finds chats by words in user and assistant messages and shows the matching text. It switches on dsh's built-in SQLite FTS5 index (off in shipped dsh) with an owner-only file at `$DSH_HOME/cache/composer-plus/session-search.db`; no own search code. Whole words only, no tool output; the first search after a start builds the index (about 15 s and about 1 GB peak Host memory for 250 chats).
- Turn rollback: Like OpenCode's undo or Claude Code's /rewind, a ↶ button on each of your messages takes that message and everything after it out of the chat and the model context (one hidden marker, the same mechanism as dsh's /compact; the log is never rewritten) and puts the message back in the composer to edit and resend. "Chat and files" also puts the project files back as they were before that message, bash changes too: the Host takes a git snapshot of the work tree before each message into a private store under `$DSH_HOME/cache/composer-plus/rollback/` (the repository's objects are read, never written; index, HEAD, refs, stash and config are untouched); only regular files inside the chat folder are written. Needs a git repository for files; the 50 newest snapshots per chat. When dsh-rewind-plugin is installed it owns rollback and Composer Plus shows no button. After a rollback, Redo starts a new chat from just before it (dsh's own fork, the same model context) and can put the files back; a file edited after the rollback is kept unless you choose to overwrite it.
- Delete chat: "Delete…" in a chat's sidebar menu (dsh itself only archives). The chat stops (dsh's own archive with stop) and its log folders, with its subagent chats, move to the macOS Trash (elsewhere `$DSH_HOME/trash`); the id stays archived, so a folder put back shows up under "Archived only" after a restart.
- Project name in the composer: the stats row under the composer (turns, tokens, cache hit) starts with the chat's project name (dsh's project title, else the folder name); the folder path is its tooltip; a click finds the chat in the sidebar (opens the sidebar, the project and Show more, scrolls to the chat, which blinks for 5 seconds).
- Input history: ↑ / ↓ in an empty composer recalls messages you sent.
- Shift+Tab plan mode: Shift+Tab adds or removes `/plan ` at the start of the draft, or leaves plan mode.
- Keep composer focus: after you send a `/` command or skill, the cursor goes back to the composer, unless a menu, a dialog or another field has the focus. (dsh makes the composer read-only while it resolves the command, and the browser removes the focus.)
- Fit question card to window: dsh's question card (`ask_user_question`) scrolls the question and its answers together, keeps Skip and Submit in view at the bottom, and uses the height of the window less 200 px. Without it, dsh caps the card at 60% of the window (at most 520 px) and scrolls only the answers, so a long question can push its own end, the answers and the buttons out of the card.
- One-click Continue: after a stopped, failed or cut-off turn the Send button becomes ▶ and resumes without a visible chat message. Queued messages stay queued: ▶ continues only the stopped task, then the queue runs.
- Resume after restart: Off by default. Chats that were working when dsh quit or closed continue by themselves at the next start; a running `/goal` round goes on with the next goal round. Chats you stopped, finished or failed chats do not continue. dsh has no built-in setting for this.
- Queue drag-and-drop: reorder queued messages by dragging the ⠿ grip or with ↑ / ↓.
- Edit queued message in place: double-click a queued message or click its Edit button to edit it in place: change the text, remove images and files (✕) or add new ones (paperclip or paste). Enter saves, Esc cancels, Shift+Enter adds a line. The message keeps its place in the queue, and the kept images and files stay as they are. The queue cannot be reordered while the editor is open. In Tether: queued message menu → Edit (a sheet).
- Copy session link: right-click a chat to copy a `dsh-session:` link that attaches it to another chat as read-only context. dsh 0.2.1's own "Copy Session ID" copies only the plain id; this item comes right after it.
- Copy message link: a 🔗 button on each message copies `dsh-session:<chat>#<message seq>`; sent in a chat (dsh 0.2.1 and later), the link is a chip that opens that chat, loads its history back to the message, scrolls to it and highlights it. dsh still attaches the linked chat as read-only context.
- Export chat as Markdown: right-click a chat (or its … menu) → Export as Markdown… → Copy to clipboard or Save .md file. The user's messages and the assistant's text replies, oldest first, with a title, the project name and the date; code blocks are kept (an open fence is closed); tool calls, thinking, hidden context and messages withdrawn by Turn rollback or dsh-rewind-plugin are left out (messages that /compact summarized stay); at most about 4 million characters. The Host route `GET /api/composer-plus.export?sessionId=` reads only the chat log.
- Copy project path: right-click a project in the sidebar → Copy path copies its full folder path.
- Project search in a new chat: the new chat project menu lists the projects A–Z and has a search box (type part of a name, Enter picks the first match); dsh's saved project order does not change.
- Default workspace for New session: the global New session button (the sidebar top button, its shortcut, the logo) always opens in one default workspace, set in Settings (a project of dsh, or dsh's general folder Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace, made on first use), not in the open or the most recent project; a project's own "+" and the new chat project menu still choose any project; the Tether iPhone app's Quick chat uses the same default.
- Find in chat: Cmd+F on macOS (Ctrl+F on Windows and Linux) opens a find box over the open chat: every match in the messages and replies that the page shows is highlighted (CSS Custom Highlight API, dsh's DOM is not changed), with n / total, next and previous (Enter, Shift+Enter, ↓, ↑, wrap-around) and Esc to close; case, accents and the Turkish dotless ı are ignored; it follows a streaming reply. Closed tool steps and history that is not loaded are not searched.
- Branch per chat: each chat can run on its own git branch: on the new chat screen the branch button (branch icon) between the project button and the mode button offers New branch, and the first message (it can carry images and files) makes the AI name the branch (a message with no text gets the dated name feat/chat-YYYYMMDD-HHMM, with no model call), creates a worktree in <project>/.worktrees/, copies the files listed in .worktreeinclude (for example .env and node_modules, never other ignored files) and opens a new chat there with the text, the images and the files; the composer takes no text while the branch is created; the open chat's header shows its branch, changes and push state.
- Branches in the workspace tree: off by default: each branch with a worktree folder in <project>/.worktrees/ shows as a project inside its project (dsh's Workspace Tree view nests it), a branch whose folder is deleted leaves the list and its chats go to Ungrouped; when the agent of a chat in the project folder creates and checks out a branch while the folder has no uncommitted changes, the project folder goes back to its branch, the branch gets its own worktree folder, and the chat moves there (a copy continues the task in the branch project, the old chat is archived); checked at start, every 30 s, after each turn and on window focus.
- Next message prediction: On by default; switch it off in Settings. After a finished turn, the empty composer shows a guess of the user's next message in that chat (Tab accepts, Esc hides); the model is chosen in Settings from dsh's own model list, default = dsh's default model; one short model call per finished turn; Tether shows it above the composer.
- Complete while typing: Off by default; switch it on in Settings. While the user types, grey text after the cursor shows how the message may go on (Tab adds it, Esc hides it); it suggests only the user's own next words (never a reply to the user, no made-up error texts or names) and shows nothing when the message looks complete or the model is not sure; its own Model menu in Settings (default: Same as Next message prediction; the choice is kept by the Host in complete.json and a model must be one that dsh lists); one model call at each pause while typing (many more tokens); not for slash commands, chips or a cursor that is not at the end; Tether shows it above the field (tap adds it).
- Improve prompt: On by default (a model call only on a click). A magic wand button in the composer's tool row rewrites the typed draft as a clearer prompt for the agent (goal first, numbered steps for several parts, the check to run), with this chat (rolled-back messages left out), the project brief (README, AGENTS.md, manifests, latest commits), git's changed files and the paths whose names match the draft as context; keeps the draft's language and never invents names. The result replaces the draft in the composer and is not sent; Cmd/Ctrl+Z (one step) or the Undo improvement button brings the typed text back; typing during the call keeps the new text; Esc or a second click cancels; one call per chat at a time. Its own Model menu in Settings (default: the chat's model; kept by the Host in improve.json, a model must be one that dsh lists). Not for slash commands or a draft with a file chip; at most 8000 characters. Tether has the wand next to the field.
- Goal check: On by default (a model call only when the agent marks a goal complete; it never starts a turn). When the model calls update_goal with action complete in an automatic /goal round, the Host (tools/pre-execute, after every other gate allowed it) first runs the project's test command (the chat's own command, else detected: package.json scripts.test with npm/pnpm/yarn/bun by lock file, Makefile test, cargo test, go test ./..., pytest; project files read only as regular files inside the chat folder) under the chat's sandbox mode; it skips the run when the agent's newest change-capable step was its own passing bash run of that exact command in the same folder (a pipe or && does not count). Then one verifier model call with no tools and a fresh context reads the goal, the chat since the goal started (rolled-back steps left out), git status and the test result, and answers pass or the missing items. A failed test (no model call then), a verifier 'not done' or a check error denies the call with the reason: the goal stays active and dsh's goal driver starts the next round. A human turn, /goal and the goal bar are not checked. Optional per-chat time and token budget: over it, the goal becomes blocked (code budget-limit) at the next idle edge; resuming starts a new budget. A row under dsh's goal bar shows the test, the last result and the budget, with Edit, Run now and Clear. Its own Model menu in Settings (default: the chat's model). Kept by the Host in goal-check.json. Not in Tether (the check runs on the Mac).
- Allow for this chat: In Auto Review approvals, allow one exact tool in one chat for a set time (Settings: 15 min / 1 h default / 4 h / 8 h / until revoked); then the agent asks again; revocable; saved across restarts.
- Project status: sidebar project rows show waiting / done / running (an unread finished chat shows its green dot also while another chat runs).
- Git branch on chat rows: Git branch on chat rows: each sidebar chat row shows the git branch of the chat's folder at its last turn (the Host records it with read-only git at each turn start and end; a detached HEAD shows its short id; no pill outside a repository, before the first turn since install, or under a project row with the same name as the branch, as for a Branch per chat worktree, except in "In one list"). The switch is kept by the Host (on by default).
- Mark all as read: a project's "…" menu in the sidebar gets "Mark all as read": one click clears dsh's unread (green) dot of every chat in that project; Tether's dots follow.
- Active projects first: a project moves to the top of the sidebar when one of its chats runs or needs you; the move is saved in dsh's project order.
- Recent projects filter: "Active in the last 2 hours" in the sidebar's view options shows only projects with a chat active in the last 2 hours; a finished chat that was not opened yet keeps its project shown.
- Collapse all projects: a sidebar header button, shown while a project is open, closes every open project.
- Order by status: "By status" in the sidebar's Order by puts finished, then running or waiting, then automated chats first in "In one list" (view only).
- Background notifications: OS notification and Dock badge when a chat finishes or really waits for an approval, a question or a plan review; click opens the chat.
- Application language: Switches the whole dsh interface to one of 11 extra languages: Türkçe, Español, Português (Brasil), Français, Deutsch, Русский, 日本語, 한국어, Bahasa Indonesia, Tiếng Việt, हिन्दी. Each pack has 3,280 texts: every UI text of dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 and 0.2.1-rc.2, the plugin's own texts and the dsh-rewind plugin.
- Mobile connect (iPhone): use dsh from the Tether iPhone app on the same Wi-Fi or over Tailscale. Switch it on in Settings → Composer Plus (off by default, it opens a network port on the Mac); a "Mobile connect" button at the bottom left shows the pairing QR code (a tether://pair link: the iPhone Camera opens it in Tether, which asks before it connects; the Mac page shows the request, a countdown and what happened). Pinned TLS, one-time pairing code approved on the Mac, hashed device tokens, RPC allowlist. The phone keeps any number of paired Macs and switches between them from a picker at the top; only the Mac on screen is connected. The Mac pairing page lists each paired iPhone with its last connection and removes one with one click (its key stops working at once); a "Tailscale only" option refuses local-network connections; an access log shows each connection attempt (time, IP, device, allowed or refused). Tether can lock itself with Face ID or the passcode (Tether Settings → Privacy). A message from the phone can carry photos from the camera, the photo library or the clipboard (the composer's + menu; at most 4, sent as JPEG attachments of the message). The iOS app source is in tether/ios.
- Automatic updates: at dsh start, installs the newest GitHub release (once it is on npm, as its exact npm tarball) through dsh's own plugin manager and notifies; dsh 0.2.1 loads it at once when no dsh settings change, otherwise restart dsh to load it. The first start that runs the installed version shows its GitHub release notes once in a closable "What's new" window (from the same update check, no extra network call).
- Backup: On by default (nothing runs without a click). Settings → Composer Plus → Backup: Back up now writes the whole dsh home into ~/Desktop/dsh-backups/dsh-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSSmmm>.tar.gz (gzip tar, one top folder) with .sha256, .meta.json and .redacted.json; the format and folder are the same as dsh-backup 0.13, so its archives stay usable. cache/, dsh-runtimes/, every node_modules and .system are not archived. Masked (not in the archive, the real copy only in composer-plus-vault/<archive>/ of the backup folder, 0600; dsh-backup archives read their secrets from its vault/ mirror): .credentials.yaml, .env and .env.*, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, qq-bridge/config.json, and in every .yml/.yaml file (also cordis.patch.yml.bak-…) the values (one line, plain or block scalar) of keys whose last word is token, secret, password, passphrase, credential(s), authorization, apiKey, accessKey, secretKey, privateKey, clientSecret, authKey or authToken (maxTokens and apiKeyEnv stay). Symbolic links are archived as links and never followed; FIFOs, sockets and devices are skipped; files are read with O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK. Per archive: Check (reads it fully, checksum, safe names), For another computer (a transfer-<time> folder with the archive, its sidecars and the rescue console, no vault: secrets are entered again there), Delete (also its vault copies). One backup action at a time (also against the rescue console: a lock file in the folder). Restore is not in dsh: quit dsh and use the rescue console. Not in Tether.
- Automatic backup: Off by default (each copy is about the size of the dsh home without its cache; the Host keeps the switch in auto-backup.json). When on, the Host backs up every 6, 12, 24 (default), 72 or 168 hours, counted from the newest full backup in the folder (also a manual one), and keeps the newest 3, 5, 7 (default) or 14 of its own automatic backups (Back up now deletes nothing; dsh-backup archives are never deleted); never in the first 45 s after a start. When dsh or Composer Plus starts with another version than at the last start, it first takes a dsh-pre-upgrade-<time> snapshot (the newest 2 stay). A failed backup shows in Settings and the next try waits 30 minutes (or the interval when shorter). Not in Tether.
- Session log check: On by default (runs only on a click). Settings → Composer Plus → Session log check → Check session logs reads the newest log of every chat under sessions/ (session[.vN].jsonl[.zstd]): zstd frames with dsh's own rules (a torn last frame is not damage: dsh cuts it at its next write), the first frame must be exactly the header line, no record may end inside a complete frame, and a row that is not JSON or (v4) has a seq other than its place is damage only when a turn/end row follows it (dsh's own recoverable rule; otherwise dsh opens the rows before it). Repair from backups checks again, then puts back each damaged log of a chat that is not open in this dsh from the newest archive that has a healthy copy; the damaged file stays as <name>.corrupt-<time>. Messages after that backup are not in the copy. Open chats: the rescue console, with dsh closed. Not in Tether.
- Rescue console: On by default (the Host keeps the switch in rescue-console.json). Each backup writes composer-plus-rescue.mjs (the same backup.mjs, Node standard library only) and a launcher (macOS: Composer Plus Rescue.command, Linux: composer-plus-rescue.sh, Windows: Composer Plus Rescue.cmd) into the backup folder; a start replaces a copy that is there. The launcher finds Node.js 18 or later on PATH, Homebrew, nvm or dsh's own runtime, else runs the DeepSeek Harness app as Node.js (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1). A terminal menu, no network port: list backups, check one, restore one, check session logs, repair them. Restore and repair refuse while dsh runs (storages/dsh-composer-plus/running/host-<pid>.json of a live process; each dsh process has its own), checks the archive, asks to type RESTORE, writes it into a new folder next to the dsh home (files O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW, symbolic links last and never followed, no entry below a link, no devices), puts the masked files back from the vault (composer-plus-vault/<archive>/, or dsh-backup's vault/ mirror for its archives), swaps the folders (the old home stays as <home>.pre-restore-<time>), moves cache/, dsh-runtimes/ and node_modules over from it, and offers pnpm install for profiles that need it. Switched off, the files are removed. Not in Tether.
<!-- END GENERATED FEATURES -->
